method.value: Spectrum extracted from each datacube with circular aperture ~1.6" centred on IRAS16293 B

evidence.quote: a spectrum was extracted from each datacube using a circular support with size $\sim$1.6$^{\prime\prime}$ centered at the position of IRAS16293 B

analysis_steps.goal: Identify lines and fit LTE CH3NCO

method.value: MADCUBAIJ synthetic LTE spectra compared with observed to derive Tex and N

evidence.quote: The comparison between the observed and the synthetic spectrum for the unblended ransitions can be used to derive the excitation temperature and total column density that best match the observations.
We assumed a linewidth of 1.1 km s$^{-1}$, and the source size was constrained by the continuum emission to 0.5$^{\prime\prime}$
MADCUBAIJ produces synthetic spectra assuming Local Thermodinamical Equilibrium (LTE) conditions.

validation.value: Checked synthetic spectrum for missing detectable transitions; lines optically thin

evidence.quote: a careful check of the synthetic spectrum was performed to confirm that no dectectable transitions were missing from our observational data.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive H2 column density and abundance

method.value: Optically thin dust continuum at 232 GHz

evidence.quote: we have derived the H$_2$ column density by using the continuum flux measured at 232 GHz (1.4$\pm$0.05 Jy within a deconvolved size of 0.55$\ensuremath{''}\times$0.47$\ensuremath{''}$)

assumptions.value: Optically thin dust, kappa 0.009 cm2/g, gas-to-dust 100, Tdust=Tex=110 K

evidence.quote: assuming optically thin dust, a dust opacity of 0.009 cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: ossenkopf94) and a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100
consistent with that estimated by (cite: jorgensen16) at higher frequencies

analysis_steps.goal: HNCO and NH2CHO columns via isotopologues

method.value: LTE fits of HNC18O (Tex fixed 110 K) and NH2 13CHO (Tex 75 K), scaled by isotopic ratios

evidence.quote: For a fixed excitation temperature of $T_{ex}$=110 K, (the $T_{ex}$ derived for CH$_3$NCO; see Section 3.1)
By assuming an isotopic ratio $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O = 500 (Wilson & Rood 1994)

method.value: Three-phase UCL_CHEM gas-grain model with added CH3NCO, HNCO routes

evidence.quote: The physical conditions and the chemical composition of the IRAS16293 B hot corino were modelled using a three phase model.

key_parameters.value: nH 5e8 cm-3, T 10 to 110 K over 1e5 yr

evidence.quote: assuming a constant H$_2$ gas density ($5\times10^{8}$ cm$^{-3}$) while gradually increasing the gas temperature from 10$\,$K to 110$\,$K during the first 10$^5$ yrs

validation.value: Compared with observed abundances and L1544 upper limits

evidence.quote: our model perfectly reproduces the upper limits of CH$_3$NCO measured in cold cores such as L1544

findings_qualitative.value: CH3NCO lines optically thin and coincident with continuum, size ~0.5"

claims.hypothesis: CH3NCO exists in a solar-type protostar
claims.experiment: LTE analysis of archival+own ALMA Band 3-6 spectra of IRAS16293 B
claims.result: 8 unblended lines, Tex 110 K, N 4.0e15 cm-2
claims.finding: CH3NCO detected in a low-mass protostar

evidence.quote: detected 8 unblended transitions of CH$_3$NCO

claims.hypothesis: CH3NCO/HNCO and /NH2CHO ratios compare with other sources
claims.experiment: Isotopologue-based columns of HNCO and NH2CHO
claims.result: Ratios ~0.08; similar to SgrB2(N) HNCO ratio, much lower than comet 67P in HNCO
claims.finding: Ratios similar to high-mass sources, differ from comet

evidence.quote: it is a factor of $\sim$50 lower than in comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko

claims.result: Grain surface alone insufficient; gas+ice reproduce within factor 4
claims.finding: Both ice and gas-phase formation required

evidence.quote: our modelling shows that formation both in the ices and in the gas phase is required to explain the observed abundance of CH$_3$NCO in IRAS16293 B
